arxiv-2302-01241.title: Diagrammatization and Abduction to Improve AI Interpretability With Domain-Aligned Explanations for Medical Diagnosis Conference: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 26–May 01, 2025; Yokohama, Japan CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI ’25), April 26–May
arxiv-2302-01241.creator: Brian Y. Lim, Joseph P. Cahaly, Chester Y. F. Sng, Adam Chew
arxiv-2302-01241.description: Abstract . Many visualizations have been developed for explainable AI (XAI), but they often require further reasoning by users to interpret. Investigating XAI for high-stakes medical diagnosis, we propose improving domain alignment with diagrammatic and abductive reasoning to reduce the interpretability gap.

arxiv-2304-01188.title: The Timing System of LIGO Discoveries
arxiv-2304-01188.creator: Andrew G. Sullivan, Yasmeen Asali, Zsuzsanna Márka, Daniel Sigg, Stefan Countryman, Imre Bartos, Keita Kawabe, Marc D. Pirello, Michael Thomas, Thomas J. Shaffer, Keith Thorne, Michael Laxen, Joseph Betzwieser, Kiwamu Izumi, Rolf Bork, Alex Ivanov, Dave Barker, Carl Adams, Filiberto Clara, Maxim Fac
arxiv-2304-01188.description: Abstract LIGO’s mission critical timing system has enabled gravitational wave and multi-messenger astrophysical discoveries as well as the rich science extracted. Achieving optimal detector sensitivity, detecting transient gravitational waves, and especially localizing gravitational wave sources, the underpinning of multi-messenger astrophysics, all require proper gravitational wave data time-stamping.

arxiv-2405-12498.title: Model independent calibration for sound horizon combining observations of supernovae and transversal BAO measurements
arxiv-2405-12498.creator: Tonghua Liu, Xinyi Zhong, Jieci Wang, Marek Biesiada
arxiv-2405-12498.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tonghua Liu, Xinyi Zhong, Jieci Wang, Marek Biesiada. The sound horizon is a key theoretical prediction of the cosmological model that depends on the speed of sound and the rate of expansion in the early universe, before matter and radiation decoupled. The standard ruler for low redshift calibration of baryon acoustic oscillations (BAOs) is a direct measurement that would exist even if the standard cosmological model and the standard assumptions of early physics did not.

arxiv-2407-14403.title: ALF: an asymmetric Lyot wavefront sensor for the ELT/METIS vortex coronagraph
arxiv-2407-14403.creator: G. Orban de Xivry, O. Absil, C. Delacroix, P. Pathak, M. Quesnel, T. Bertram
arxiv-2407-14403.description: Abstract Non-common path quasi-static and differential aberrations are one of the big hurdles of direct imaging for current and future high-contrast imaging instruments. They increase speckle and photon noise thus reducing the achievable contrast and lead to a significant hit in HCI performance.

arxiv-2512-13122.title: DePT3R: Joint Dense Point Tracking and 3D Reconstruction of Dynamic Scenes in a Single Forward Pass
arxiv-2512-13122.creator: Vivek Alumootil, Tuan-Anh Vu, M. Khalid Jawed
arxiv-2512-13122.description: Abstract Current methods for dense 3D point tracking in dynamic scenes typically rely on pairwise processing, require known camera poses, or assume a temporal ordering to input frames, constraining their flexibility and applicability. Additionally, recent advances have successfully enabled efficient 3D reconstruction from large-scale, unposed image collections, underscoring opportunities for unified approaches to dynamic scene understanding.

britannica-1911-pardaillan.title: Pardaillan (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-pardaillan.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-pardaillan.description: Article 'Pardaillan' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 20), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. of which several members distinguished themselves in the service of the kings of France in the 16th and 17th centuries. Antoine Arnaud de Pardaillan, maréchal de camp, served Henri IV. in Franche-Comté, Picardy and Savoy, and was created marquis de Montespan in 1612 and marquis d’Antin in 1615 under Louis XIII. His grandson Louis Henri, marquis de Montespan, the mistress of Louis XIV.

pmc-10620492.title: E-Health Interventions for Older Adults With Frailty: A Systematic Review
pmc-10620492.creator: Hyeong-Wook Han, Si-Woon Park, Doo Young Kim, Bum-Suk Lee, Daham Kim, Namo Jeon, Yun-Jung Yang
pmc-10620492.description: ObjectiveTo systematically review the efficacy of e-Health interventions on physical performance, activity and quality of life in older adults with sarcopenia or frailty.MethodsA systematic review was conducted by searching the MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Library, CINHAL, Web of Science, and the Physiotherapy Evidence Database for experimental studies published in English from 1990 to 2021.

pmc-11342656.title: Intestinal parasitic co-infections associated with Helicobacter pylori among paediatric patients with gastrointestinal illness attending a general hospital in southern Ethiopia
pmc-11342656.creator: Addis Aklilu, Melat Woldemariam, Edilu Wanke, Mohammed Seid, Aseer Manilal, Javed Masood Khan, Idhayadhulla Akbar
pmc-11342656.description: BackgroundConcurrent infections or co-infections caused by intestinal parasites and Helicobacter pylori are quite rampant in paediatrics living in endemic areas of sub-Saharan Africa, including Ethiopia, and if left untreated, can result in severe complications and hence must be addressed to ensure their health and well-being.ObjectivesTo determine the prevalence of intestinal parasitic and H.

pmc-11396819.title: In Situ Antimicrobial Properties of Sabinene Hydrate, a Secondary Plant Metabolite
pmc-11396819.creator: Asta Judžentienė, Dalė Pečiulytė, Irena Nedveckytė
pmc-11396819.description: The objective of this research was to investigate natural products for their potential against pathogenic microorganisms. Sabinene hydrate (SH), a monoterpenoid, is synthesised by numerous different plants as a secondary metabolite. At present, there is a lack of definite investigations regarding the antimicrobial activity of SH itself and its different isomers.

pmc-11519588.title: Half-quantum mirror Hall effect
pmc-11519588.creator: Bo Fu, Kai-Zhi Bai, Shun-Qing Shen
pmc-11519588.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We predict a half-quantized mirror Hall effect induced by mirror symmetry in strong topological insulator films. These films are known to host a pair of gapless Dirac cones in the first Brillouin zone associated with surface electrons. Our findings reveal that mirror symmetry assigns a unique mirror parity to each Dirac cone, resulting in a half-quantized Hall conductance of ±e22h for each cone.

pmc-11588829.title: Ruxolitinib for steroid-refractory chronic graft-versus-host disease: Japanese subgroup analysis of REACH3 study
pmc-11588829.creator: Souichi Shiratori, Kentaro Fukushima, Yasushi Onishi, Noriko Doki, Tatsunori Goto, Masaya Okada, Hirohisa Nakamae, Yoshinobu Maeda, Koji Kato, Takayuki Ishikawa, Tadakazu Kondo, Masako Toyosaki, Takashi Ikeda, Naoyuki Uchida, Akio Maki, Fumika Shimada, Takeshi Tajima, Tommaso Stefanelli, Takanori Te
pmc-11588829.description: Ruxolitinib, a Janus kinase (JAK1–JAK2) inhibitor, has demonstrated safety and efficacy in patients with graft-versus-host disease (GvHD). This phase 3 randomized trial (REACH3) evaluated the efficacy and the safety of ruxolitinib 10 mg twice daily compared with investigator-selected best available therapy (BAT) in a subgroup of Japanese patients (n = 37) with steroid-refractory or dependent (SR/D) chronic GvHD.

pmc-12416534.title: Transcriptomic Changes Across the HPG Axis Following Prenatal Exposure to the EDC Mixture NeuroMix
pmc-12416534.creator: Tyler M Milewski, Madeline Streifer, Lindsay M Thompson, Dana Sheinhaus, Andrew Hynes, Andrea C Gore
pmc-12416534.description: Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) are exogenous chemicals that are ubiquitous in our environment and found in everyday items. We previously reported that prenatal exposure of rats to a human-relevant mixture of EDCs, NeuroMix (NMX), led to alterations in physiological and behavioral phenotypes.

pmc-12592612.title: Combined CHK1 and PD-L1 blockade as a novel therapeutic strategy against stemness and immunosuppression in ovarian cancer
pmc-12592612.creator: Mengqing Chen, Lin Huang, Mengna Zhu, Jing Cai, Feiquan Ying, Lin Liu, Wenhan Li, Si Sun, Yiping Wen
pmc-12592612.description: BackgroundCancer stem cells (CSCs) are considered the ‘seeds’ of recurrence after chemotherapy, but eliminating CSCs remains notoriously challenging. This study aims to examine whether cell cycle checkpoint kinase 1 (CHK1) blockade can abrogate the stemness of ovarian cancer (OC) cells, making them easier targets of anti-tumor immunity.

pmc-12614963.title: Determining the Importance of the Stringent Response for Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Virulence In Vivo
pmc-12614963.creator: Naznin R Choudhury, Lucy Urwin, Bartłomiej Salamaga, Lynne R Prince, Stephen A Renshaw, Rebecca M Corrigan
pmc-12614963.description: The stringent response is a stress signaling pathway with links to bacterial virulence. This pathway is controlled by the nucleotide alarmone (p)ppGpp, produced in Staphylococcus aureus by 3 synthetase enzymes. Here, we used a panel of synthetase mutants to examine the importance of this signaling network for S. aureus survival and virulence in vivo.

pmc-12723070.title: Thermal Tolerance Varies Latitudinally and Broadly Mirrors Genetic Structure in the Seaweed Phyllospora comosa Across Its Entire Latitudinal Range
pmc-12723070.creator: Rosalie J Harris, Callum Bryant, Andrea Leigh, Melinda A Coleman, Adrienne B Nicotra, Georgina Wood
pmc-12723070.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Climate‐driven warming is causing rapid changes in marine environments, contracting ranges and reshaping ecosystems. Understanding how genetic structure and phenotypic variation interact to determine populations' ability to tolerate warming aids in predicting biogeographic shifts and informs conservation. We tested whether photosynthetic thermal tolerance in the habitat‐forming seaweed Phyllospora comosa reflects underlying genetic differentiation across its full latitudinal range in south‐eastern Australia. We sampled 15 male and 15 female individuals at replicate sites representing three previously defined genetic groups.

pmc-13025973.title: Nerve-Sparing in High-Risk Prostate Cancer: Advantages and Pitfalls of Current Strategies and Technologies
pmc-13025973.creator: Daniele Robesti, Pierluigi Russo, Giuseppe Fallara, Fernando Blank, Massimo Valerio, Ashutosh K. Tewari, Francesco Montorsi, Guillaume Ploussard, Nilesh Patil, Alberto Martini
pmc-13025973.description: Simple SummaryHigh-risk prostate cancer carries a relevant risk of positive surgical margins after radical prostatectomy, which may lead to disease recurrence and the need for additional treatments. At the same time, preserving the neurovascular bundles is crucial to maintain postoperative sexual function, even in selected high-risk patients.

pmc-13037295.title: Association of lymph node ratio with adjuvant radiotherapy benefit in human papillomavirus-positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma: a population-based analysis
pmc-13037295.creator: Zhen-Zhen Lu, Xin-Jia Chen, Zi-Qing You, Yi-Min Li, San-Gang Wu
pmc-13037295.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeTo analyze the prognostic value of lymph node ratio (LNR, number of metastatic nodes divided by total nodes excised) and to determine whether LNR can guide treatment decisions in human papillomavirus (HPV)-related oropharyngeal carcinoma (OPC).MethodsWe retrospectively included HPV-related OPC who underwent surgery and lymph node dissection between 2010 and 2020 using the data from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results program.

pmc-13180272.title: Pilot testing of a brief pre-consultation medicines adherence tool in a geriatric outpatient setting
pmc-13180272.creator: Jennifer M Stevenson, Massimo Pezzolato, Sarah Chapman, Aiman Ibrahim, Tae Ibrahim, Nabeel Syed, John A Weinman
pmc-13180272.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionIn older adults, medication non-adherence is prevalent and harmful. Current methods of identification have limitations, with direct questioning often being met with a reluctance to ‘admit’ non-adherence to healthcare professionals. The Making Medicines Work for You (MMWFY) tool consists of seven items (mapped to recognised adherence barriers) and a free-text box, and has been developed to support patients and clinicians identify and discuss adherence issues in a clinical setting.

pmc-13196213.title: Genome-resolved multi-omics provide new insights into microbial nitrogen utilization by the rumen microbiota
pmc-13196213.creator: Ming Yan, Jeffrey Firkins, Jiarong Guo, Alejandro Relling, Zhongtang Yu
pmc-13196213.description: BackgroundOptimizing nitrogen (N) utilization in ruminant production systems holds both economic and environmental significance. However, traditional paradigms of N metabolism, derived primarily from well-studied model rumen bacteria, do not fully reflect the diverse and complex N metabolism in the rumen ecosystem.

pmc-13257365.title: Developmental Programming of Drug Response: Microbiota as a Missing Dimension in Perinatal Drug Discovery
pmc-13257365.creator: Yanan Zhang, Liangkun Ma, Yan Wang
pmc-13257365.description: Drug exposure during pregnancy and early life is typically considered a short-term clinical intervention rather than a determinant of long-term pharmacological outcomes. Consequently, the developmental context is largely absent from drug discovery and drug development paradigms, where efficacy, safety and target engagement are evaluated predominantly in adult, steady-state systems.

pmc-13317216.title: Insights into Aspergillus fumigatus morphogenesis and pathogenesis through the putative lipid transporter ArvA
pmc-13317216.creator: Cecilia Gutierrez-Perez, Jane T. Jones, Charles T. S. Puerner, Sandeep Vellanki, Nicole E. Kordana, Matthew R. James, Elisa M. Vesely, Angus Johnson, Robert A. Cramer
pmc-13317216.description: Aspergillus fumigatus poses a significant threat to human well-being, in part due to the increasing emergence of strains resistant to frontline antifungal therapy. In this study, we observed that the gene arvA is required for A. fumigatus morphogenesis, antifungal drug susceptibility, and cell wall homeostasis. Intriguingly, our study reveals novel morphological and growth aberrations in the absence of arvA.

pmc-13560098.title: Analysis of the Role of N‐Linked Glycans on Human CD1d Molecules
pmc-13560098.creator: Syamdas Bandyopadhyay, Sayantan Pradhan
pmc-13560098.description: CD1d is a cell‐surface expressed glycoprotein that presents a variety of lipid and glycolipid antigens to invariant natural killer T‐cells (iNKT). We have examined the role of the N‐linked glycans on the human CD1d (hCD1d) in modulating the responses of iNKT cells using a combination of cell‐free, cell‐based assays and in silico analyses.

pmc-13570882.title: Reply to ‘The method matters: free water imaging in Parkinson’s disease is not a binary verdict’
pmc-13570882.creator: Yun Hwa Roh, Jinyoung Youn, Sang-Young Kim, Hwan Heo, Soohwa Song, Beomseok Sohn
pmc-13570882.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). We reply to the Matters Arising on our study comparing neuromelanin and free water imaging for early Parkinson’s disease diagnosis. The authors raised considerations regarding image registration, age imbalance, repetition time, and conceptual framing. We clarify that our registration pipeline is validated for subcortical structures, that age does not account for neuromelanin’s superior performance, and that our acquisition parameters meet recommended standards.

pmc-13580621.title: Con-sequins 2026: From mission to momentum
pmc-13580621.creator: Edwin Akomaning, Carol Joseph, Iris Ovbiagele, Raelle Tagge
pmc-13580621.description: A foundational challenge of equity neuroscience is understanding how to move from describing inequitable neurological disparities to identifying the mechanisms, systems, and infrastructures needed to reduce them. The Society for Equity Neuroscience (SEQUINS) was founded in 2024 to advance brain health equity and reduce neurological disparities through science [1].

pmc-13635945.title: Intact Cell Dissociation of Formalin-Fixed Paraffin-Embedded Colon Tissue Enhances Cell Recovery and Gene Detection in Single-Cell RNA Sequencing
pmc-13635945.creator: James R. Evans, Alan J. Simmons, Zhengyi Chen, Monica E. Brown, Matthew E. Bechard, Morad C. Malek, Cody N. Heiser, Frank Revetta, M. Kay Washington, Laura P. Hale, Robert J. Coffey, Ken S. Lau
pmc-13635945.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Graphical abstract

Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has transformed the understanding of tissue heterogeneity at a cellular resolution.1 However, its application to archived human specimens, particularly formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue, remains limited despite the widespread clinical use of FFPE preservation.
